executive_summary.headline: Media tools get faster and cheaper: Images 2.6 and Omni 1.2 Flash
executive_summary.body: ChatGPT Images 2.6 adds GIFs, SVG export and saved references on every tier, and Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash makes 15-second videos at $0.07 a second, with three free clips a month in Google Vids.

executive_summary.headline: Claude reads your bank history, and Splice and Instagram put assistants in the editor
executive_summary.body: Claude Personal Finance analyzes two years of linked transactions for US Pro, Max and Ultra users. Splice Create is a Mac DAW in beta, free to start, with the Rheo assistant built in, and Instagram Edits for Mac exports 4K without a watermark and accepts agents through MCP.

executive_summary.headline: Science models arrive in open form
executive_summary.body: Deep Principle's MIT-licensed Hydrogen-1.0 scores 38.3% on FrontierScience-Research, DeepMind adds Cheminformatics Skills to Antigravity with free access for 10,000 scientists, and OpenAI describes a two-person hardware design loop that finished in under a week.

executive_summary.headline: Agents move onto real phones and Macs
executive_summary.body: Glasshand rents physical iPhones to agents, Phone Harness drives iPhone and Android, Cyclon preorders an AI phone, and AWS Kiro bots and Perplexity Teammates keep agents running between sessions.

executive_summary.headline: Fun finds: a free detective game and a 2B image model trained for $21K
executive_summary.body: Uncracked City has you cross-examine LLM suspects, Linum trained a 2B image model for $21,038 under Apache 2.0, and Subvocal glasses reached 843 points on Hacker News.

top_picks.title: OpenAI ships Images 2.6 in ChatGPT, Codex and the API with animated GIFs, SVG export and saved references
top_picks.summary: Images 2.6 is available in ChatGPT on every tier, in Codex and in the API as GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and Sunburst. OpenAI says generation is 50% faster, and Flare can return an image in as little as 6 seconds at low quality. New tools add animated GIFs, SVG export, markup editing and saved reference images that you recall with an @name tag. OpenAI says people create 4 billion images a week.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: save your logo, product shots and brand colors as named references, then ask for a week of social posts as GIFs and SVGs in one session.
top_picks.competitive_context: Images 2.6 moves from single images to a reusable asset workflow: saved references, markup edits and vector export sit in one chat. The launch post does not publish API pricing for the two new models.
top_picks.pricing: Included on all ChatGPT tiers; API pricing for GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and Sunburst is not stated in the launch post.
key_takeaways: Available on all ChatGPT tiers, in Codex and in the API.
Generation is 50% faster; Flare can finish in 6 seconds at low quality.
Adds animated GIFs, SVG export, markup editing and saved @references.

top_picks.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash makes 15-second videos with conversational edits at $0.07 a second, and Google Vids gets it free
top_picks.summary: Omni 1.2 Flash generates native 15-second video, up from 10 seconds, supports multi-turn conversational editing and follows reference images more closely. It costs $0.07 per second at 720p, 30% less than Omni 1.1, and is generally available in the Gemini API and Gemini for business. Google Vids gives any Google account up to three 15-second videos a month at no cost.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: open Google Vids and turn your next product announcement into a 15-second clip, then refine it with follow-up prompts instead of regenerating.
top_picks.competitive_context: At $0.07 per second a 15-second clip costs about $1.05 at 720p, and the Vids tier removes cost entirely for light use. Multi-turn editing keeps a scene across revisions, which one-shot generators do not.
top_picks.pricing: $0.07 per second at 720p via the Gemini API (30% below Omni 1.1); Google Vids includes up to three 15-second videos a month free.
key_takeaways: Native 15-second video, up from 10 seconds.
$0.07 per second at 720p, 30% cheaper than Omni 1.1.
Free in Google Vids: three 15-second videos a month on any Google account.

top_picks.title: Claude Personal Finance reads two years of linked bank transactions and answers spending questions in chat
top_picks.summary: Personal Finance is a beta that links accounts through Plaid with read-only access and pulls up to two years of transactions into Claude. It is rolling out to Pro, Max and Ultra subscribers in the US. Claude can analyze spending, find recurring charges and answer budget questions in conversation.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: link one account, ask for every subscription charged in the last 24 months, and cancel the ones you no longer use.
top_picks.competitive_context: Claude joins budgeting apps and bank assistants by putting a long transaction history inside a general chat, so questions are open-ended rather than limited to preset reports.
top_picks.pricing: Included with Pro, Max and Ultra plans in the US; no separate fee stated.
key_takeaways: Read-only account linking through Plaid.
Up to two years of transaction history.
Beta for Pro, Max and Ultra subscribers in the US.

top_picks.title: Splice Create is a Mac music studio in beta, free to start, with millions of Splice sounds and the Rheo assistant built in
top_picks.summary: Splice Create is a standalone Mac DAW in beta, available free with no time limit, with millions of Splice sounds, instruments and effects built in and support for your own plugins and sample folders. Rheo is Create's AI assistant: Splice says it can search the catalog for human-made samples, write a MIDI pattern, work with Variations and walk you through production steps, and it does not generate new sounds. Exporting projects and licensing samples need a subscription according to Splice's FAQ and Help Center; Create Pro is $9.99 a month at introductory pricing and includes 1,000 Rheo units a month, and free accounts get 100 intro units. Splice's plans table also lists 'Export WAV and stems' under the Free card, which conflicts with those statements. Windows and web versions are listed as coming soon.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: ask Rheo to write a MIDI pattern for a 20-second jingle, build it out with catalog samples, and use it as the sound for your next video.

secondary_urls.label: Splice Help Center: Can I use Create for free?
Splice Help Center: Which plan should I choose

top_picks.competitive_context: Create puts a licensed sample library and an assistant inside the editor where tracks are made, so search, arrange and export happen in one app. Splice says Rheo does not generate new sounds; it searches, writes MIDI, works with Variations and teaches steps.
top_picks.pricing: App free with no time limit; Create Pro $9.99 a month introductory (export, sample licensing, 1,000 Rheo units a month); free accounts get 100 intro Rheo units; 1,000-unit add-ons $4.99 for Pro and $9.99 for Creator and Creator+. Splice's plans card lists WAV and stem export as free while its FAQ and Help Center require a subscription.
key_takeaways: Mac beta now; Windows and web are listed as coming soon.
Rheo searches the catalog, writes MIDI and guides production steps; it does not generate new sounds.
Export needs a subscription per Splice's FAQ and Help Center; the Free plan card lists export, a conflict on Splice's own page.

top_picks.title: DeepMind adds Cheminformatics Skills to Antigravity and offers 10,000 scientists six months of top-tier access free
top_picks.summary: Cheminformatics Skills run inside Google Antigravity through its Science plugin and build on RDKit, ChEMBL and PubChem. An agent curates literature and compound data, models molecular properties and proposes rigidified macrocycles with synthesis routes in about an hour, on a workflow that normally takes days per iteration. Google offers 10,000 scientists its highest usage tier free for six months, with applications open. Science bonus applied to the score.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: pick one design loop your lab repeats weekly, hand the data-curation and first-pass proposals to the agent, and compare cycle time after two rounds.
top_picks.competitive_context: DeepMind packages domain tools as installable agent skills instead of a closed model, so chemists reuse standard open databases. Google states that computational designs are hypotheses that still need synthesis and assay data.
top_picks.pricing: Free highest usage tier for 10,000 selected scientists for six months; enterprise sign-in with Google Cloud credentials.
key_takeaways: Skills built on RDKit, ChEMBL and PubChem.
Macrocycle proposals with synthesis routes in about an hour versus days per iteration.
Applications are open for the free six-month tier.

top_picks.title: Deep Principle releases Hydrogen-1.0, an MIT-licensed science model that scores 38.3% on FrontierScience-Research
top_picks.summary: Hydrogen-1.0 is an open-weight model post-trained from GLM-5.3 on chemistry, materials and life-science data, with 753B parameters, a 1M-token context and MIT-licensed BF16 weights on Hugging Face. The company says it scores 38.33% on FrontierScience-Research against 33.33% for GPT-6 Astra, 29.72% for Kimi K3 and 24.44% for GLM-5.3. On a materials task it predicts a HOMO-LUMO gap of 4.318 eV against 3.689 eV for GPT-6 Astra. A hosted API runs through NeuroSpark and the model powers the Mira AI Scientist app. Science bonus applied to the score.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: download the weights or try the hosted API on a materials or molecule question from your own backlog and compare it with your current general model.

secondary_urls.label: Deep Principle launch post on X (Nov 2)

top_picks.competitive_context: An open model that beats larger closed models on a science benchmark, per Deep Principle, so labs can run it on their own data. Benchmarks are the company's own. The company's launch post on X is dated November 2 and says the weights are being released; the blog post itself is undated.
top_picks.pricing: Free MIT-licensed weights on Hugging Face and ModelScope; hosted API through NeuroSpark, price not stated.
key_takeaways: 753B parameters, 1M-token context, MIT-licensed BF16 weights.
38.33% on FrontierScience-Research versus 33.33% for GPT-6 Astra, per the company.
Powers the Mira AI Scientist app.

top_picks.title: OpenAI engineers designed a Codex hardware device in under a week with GPT-6 Astra
top_picks.summary: Two OpenAI staff designed an enclosure, circuit board and firmware for a Codex device in under a week, and a contract manufacturer built prototypes in under a month. OpenAI says token use by its hardware teams is up 23-fold since February. The post states that Astra did not consistently account for manufacturer limits on its own. Science and engineering bonus applied to the score.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: ask a model to draft the enclosure, board layout and firmware for a small gadget you have wanted, then send the files to a prototype shop and time the loop.
top_picks.competitive_context: OpenAI reports a full hardware loop, from CAD to firmware to prototype, run by two people. The post says manufacturer constraints were not consistently handled by Astra, so human review stays in the loop.
key_takeaways: Two staff produced enclosure, PCB and firmware in under a week.
Prototypes built by a contract manufacturer in under a month.
Hardware-team token usage is up 23-fold since February.

top_picks.title: Thinking Machines launches Inkling 2 Small, a 594B mixture-of-experts model that scores 86.3% on SWE-Bench Pro v2 Hard
top_picks.summary: Inkling 2 Small is a 594B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 17B active parameters and image input. It scores 31 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and 86.3% on SWE-Bench Pro v2 Hard, per the company. It runs on Tinker with closed weights at first, and the company says Apache 2.0 weights follow the next week. An autoresearch example cost $426 against a $500 budget.
top_picks.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: queue a long coding or research task for the Apache 2.0 weights release next week and compare cost per finished task with your current model.
top_picks.competitive_context: Active parameters of 17B keep serving cost low for a model of this size, and the planned Apache 2.0 weights would put it among the larger permissively licensed releases. Scores are the company's own.
top_picks.pricing: Available on Tinker; per-token price not captured. Apache 2.0 weights planned the following week.
key_takeaways: 594B total, 17B active, image input.
86.3% on SWE-Bench Pro v2 Hard, per the company.
Apache 2.0 weights planned the following week.

sections.title: Product Hunt
sections.description: Top AI launches of the week by Product Hunt score, with the maker site first and the Product Hunt page second. Scores are weekly leaderboard figures at fetch time; ChatGPT Images 2.6 also placed on the board and appears in Top Picks.

items.title: Beacon turns coding-agent sessions into reusable skills across 20+ tools
items.summary: Beacon is open-source memory for coding agents. It captures sessions across Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and more than 20 other harnesses, finds repeated workflows, corrections and debugging patterns, and serves them back as skills through MCP or Agent Skills. Maker Asymptote Labs lists a $5.5 million seed round. Score and comments are the Product Hunt weekly leaderboard figures at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: install Beacon on one repo this week and see which of your repeated corrections it turns into a skill.

items.title: Wanaka Studio builds playable 3D games from a text description
items.summary: Wanaka is an AI 3D game studio. Describe a game, get a playable build, adjust it, and share a browser link so anyone can play. A free option is advertised. Score and comments are the Product Hunt weekly leaderboard figures at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: describe a ten-second reaction game for your next team offsite and send the browser link.

items.title: Scalekit AgentKit gives agents one MCP gateway to 600+ connectors
items.summary: AgentKit connects agents to more than 30,000 tools across 600+ connectors through one MCP gateway. It handles authentication, scoped access and call logs, and supports custom connectors, triggers and virtual MCP servers. Free to start with no credit card. Score and comments are the Product Hunt weekly leaderboard figures at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: wire one agent to your calendar and CRM through a single gateway and compare it with your current per-app setup.

items.title: Glasshand rents real iPhones and Macs that agents control through an API
items.summary: Glasshand provides dedicated physical iPhones and Macs that AI agents operate through an API: view the screen, tap, type and click. Uses include app testing, development and account work. Rentals run month to month. Score and comments are the Product Hunt weekly leaderboard figures at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: hand an agent a real iPhone to run your app's sign-up flow and record the screens it sees.

items.title: Teamily AI is a messenger where people and agents share context and memory
items.summary: Teamily is an AI-native messenger where people and agents chat, collaborate and automate work across studios, groups and devices with shared context and memory. Free, Pro and Team plans are listed. Score and comments are the Product Hunt weekly leaderboard figures at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: start a group with two friends and one agent and plan a trip in a single shared thread.

items.title: UnleashX lets teams hire AI employees for sales, support, finance and operations
items.summary: UnleashX is an AI workforce platform where teams hire prebuilt AI employees or build their own. They connect to CRMs and business tools, update records and work around the clock under team control. Score and comments are the Product Hunt weekly leaderboard figures at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: give one AI employee the job of updating CRM notes after every call for a week.

items.title: Floot Payments lets apps built in ChatGPT or Claude take real payments
items.summary: Floot connects to Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor to build apps with backend, database and hosting included, then publish them to the web and app stores. Payments add checkout to those apps. Plans are flat rather than per token. Score and comments are the Product Hunt weekly leaderboard figures at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: build a one-page paid tool, such as a template shop, in a chat and charge for it the same day.

items.title: Xmind 2027 adds an agent that researches and reshapes mind maps
items.summary: Xmind Agent uses your documents and maps to research ideas, compare options and refine a map in conversation. MCP connects maps to ChatGPT and Claude. Free options are available and no credit card is required. Score and comments are the Product Hunt weekly leaderboard figures at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: drop a long article into Xmind and ask the agent for a map of the three decisions it implies.

items.title: Prelulu lets you text, call and video chat with original AI characters
items.summary: Prelulu offers original AI characters that remember you, for roleplay and interactive stories, with text, voice and video chat plus character discovery across genres. Free to start. Score and comments are the Product Hunt weekly leaderboard figures at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: try a story character as a language practice partner for ten minutes a day.

items.title: Rerun gives you AI Coworkers on their own cloud computers for $29 a month
items.summary: Rerun runs AI Coworkers on their own cloud computers, on demand, on schedules or from triggers, using your connected apps and models. Coworkers can work together and pause for approval before consequential actions. $29 a month covers unlimited Coworkers, with a 5-day $0 trial. Score and comments are the Product Hunt weekly leaderboard figures at fetch time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: set a Coworker on a Monday-morning schedule to compile last week's inbox into a one-page brief.

sections.title: Frontier and Open Models
sections.description: New model releases beyond the Top Picks: Kimi K3.1 Pro weights and Linum's low-cost image model.

items.title: Moonshot releases Kimi K3.1 Pro weights: 2.8T parameters, 104B active, 1M-token context
items.summary: Moonshot published the Kimi K3.1 Pro weights on Hugging Face after announcing the model on October 25. The multimodal agentic model has 2.8T total and 104B active parameters, a 1,048,576-token context and an API with OpenAI and Anthropic-compatible endpoints. The model card lists Terminal-Bench 4.0 at 65.7, SWE Marathon v1.1 at 51.7, HLE-Full with tools at 70.0 and GPQA-Diamond at 94.2. It ships under the Kimi K3.1 Pro License, with Together AI listed as an inference provider.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: run the same five agentic tasks through Kimi K3.1 Pro on Together AI and your current model and compare cost per finished task.
items.recurrence_note: Model announced October 25; the open weights shipped this week.
items.competitive_context: One of the largest open-weight agentic models, at 104B active parameters. Benchmark figures come from the model card.
items.pricing: API at platform.kimi.ai; price not stated on the model card.

items.title: Linum trains a 2B text-to-image model for $21,038 and releases it under Apache 2.0
items.summary: P-JiT is a 2-billion-parameter text-to-image model trained in 8,415 H100-hours for $21,038, released under Apache 2.0. The Show HN post reached 284 points.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: fine-tune P-JiT on your own product photos over a weekend and compare it with a hosted image API.
items.competitive_context: A usable image model at a five-figure training bill puts from-scratch training within reach of small labs and hobbyists.

sections.title: YC and Startups
sections.description: Launch YC and Launch HN companies from the week. YC dates come from page timestamps because the pages show relative times.

items.title: Audora turns any story or book into an audiobook with a distinct voice for every character
items.summary: Audora converts a pasted story link or an uploaded file into an audiobook with a separate voice for each character. The first preview is free with no account. Audora says 10,000 readers and authors are on its waitlist, and notes that professional narration runs hundreds of dollars an hour.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: paste a favorite short story and listen to it with a cast.

items.title: Yam players logged 1 million hours in AI-powered romance simulation games
items.summary: Yam is a web platform for creating and playing AI romance simulation games with evolving worlds and AI characters. Beta players have spent 1 million hours on the platform since YC, and daily active users average more than 3 hours a day. iOS and Android apps are coming.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: study the 3-hours-a-day engagement and build a small branching story game for your own audience.

items.title: Canos detects and tracks cancer in dogs from a small blood tube with 91% sensitivity
items.summary: Canos is a liquid biopsy that uses whole-genome cell-free DNA to find and track cancer in dogs. On 896 samples from 341 dogs, Canos reports 91% sensitivity and 95% specificity. It is onboarding 10 founding clinics and mobile vets in New York City and the Bay Area. The founders' earlier company raised $3.3 million. Science bonus applied to the score.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: ask your vet whether a founding-clinic slot is open near you.

items.title: Taan AI follows 80.1% of timing instructions in music, against 28.9% for ElevenLabs
items.summary: Taan is a controllable music foundation model that takes multimodal input and is available through an API and at app.taan.ai as v1-preview. On 250 timing prompts, Taan followed 80.1% of instructions against 28.9% for ElevenLabs, 23.9% for Google Lyria and 22.0% for Suno. The v1-preview is tuned for orchestral and cinematic music, with more genres planned.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: score a 30-second trailer with a prompt that names exact hit points and check whether the music lands on them.

items.title: Momentic Mo found 269 bugs against 86 for Codex in a 60-minute QA benchmark
items.summary: Momentic is an AI QA engineer for web, iOS and Android apps. Mo finds bugs with repro steps and recordings, turns approved flows into regression tests and runs on PRs, schedules or CI. In a 60-minute benchmark Mo found 269 bugs against 86 for Codex, and the QA Bench is MIT-licensed. Free to start with no credit card.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: point Mo at your app's sign-up flow for 15 minutes and read the bug list.

items.title: Kino puts a free agent-ready video editor and media library in one app
items.summary: Kino (YC S23) is a video editor and media manager where teammates and agents work on the same timeline, including 250GB ProRes clips from local storage. More than five agents edited its launch video timeline at once. The full editor is free and Pro costs $25 per editor per month.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: invite an agent to your next edit and give it the rough-cut pass.

sections.title: Consumer, Creator and Small Business
sections.description: Everyday AI features, creator tools and fun finds worth trying this month.

items.title: Gemini turns a photo of a sketch into a working app in Canvas
items.summary: Upload a photo of a sketch to Gemini, choose Canvas, and ask 'Can you code this app?'. Gemini builds an interactive version you can test and adjust in the preview.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: sketch a three-screen tool on paper, photograph it and have a clickable version before lunch.

items.title: Instagram Edits for Mac is free, exports watermark-free 4K and lets AI agents edit through MCP
items.summary: Edits for Mac has a multi-track timeline, keyframes, color tools and automatic captions, with watermark-free 4K export and direct publishing to Instagram. Saved audio and text styles sync from the mobile app. Meta says AI agents can drive edits through MCP. Free on macOS only.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: let an agent cut your next reel's captions and first rough cut, then finish the edit by hand.

items.title: OpusClip 4.0 edits raw talking video into finished clips and ships a ChatGPT and Claude plugin
items.summary: OpusClip 4.0 turns raw footage or links into finished videos with speech cleanup, captions and B-roll, plus reusable Recipes, Viral Hook and Motion Graphics. An AI Producer plugin works from ChatGPT or Claude. The company offers 40% off the first month of Pro.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: feed your last long interview in and ask for three 60-second clips with a hook each.

items.title: Suno lets Pro and Premier users upload MIDI and have songs follow the notes exactly
items.summary: Drag a .mid or .midi file into Create and prompt Suno to follow its notes exactly or expand them with new instrumentation. At launch it works in Simple Create with v6-wild for Pro and Premier subscribers, and supports up to 16 channels with 120 controller lanes each.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: hum a melody into a phone piano app, export MIDI and have Suno arrange it as a full track.

items.title: Meta's Muse agent now takes video calls through a customizable avatar for US users
items.summary: Muse Voice lets US users call and video chat with Muse through an animated, customizable avatar built on Muse Realtime Avatar and Muse Realtime Voice. It runs on mobile, web and Mac. Meta says AI Glasses and a Muse wearable are planned, with the device due before year end.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: run a practice interview with the avatar and review how it follows your answers.

items.title: Uncracked City is a free detective game where you cross-examine LLM suspects who may lie
items.summary: Players search locations in real cities, question LLM-powered suspects, spot lies and file reports. It is free in the browser, supports six languages and has five training levels before unsolved cases. The Show HN post reached 127 points.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: play the Salem case with four suspects and see whether you catch the liar in three reports.

sections.title: Enterprise AI
sections.description: Platform launches from the large vendors, kept short.

items.title: AWS makes Kiro bots generally available as persistent agents for recurring development jobs
items.summary: Kiro bots are persistent agents in Kiro Crew that handle recurring development work, coordinate worker sessions and keep assignment-specific context. Kiro Free includes 50 credits, Pro is $20 a month for 1,000 credits, and higher tiers cost $40, $100 or $200 a month. Extra credits cost $0.04 each.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: assign a bot your weekly dependency-update job and review the pull request it opens each Monday.
items.pricing: Free 50 credits; Pro $20 a month for 1,000 credits; $40, $100 and $200 tiers; extra credits $0.04 each.

items.title: Mistral Studio launches for building agents and workflows in cloud, VPC or on premises
items.summary: Studio is Mistral's platform for building and deploying agents, workflows and apps with Mistral Large 4. It runs in cloud, private VPC, on-premises or mixed setups. Mistral cites one workflow that saves about 35 hours a week and says logistics processes reach production in weeks.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: map one 35-hour-a-week manual workflow in your team and rebuild it as an agent flow.

items.title: Microsoft Copilot Studio adds persistent agents, a customer conversation harness and spend controls
items.summary: Copilot Studio skills in Cowork are open through the Frontier program to users with a Microsoft 365 license. Persistent agents are in private preview, the customer conversation harness and cost management in the Microsoft 365 admin center are in preview, and Work IQ plus three workflow enhancements are generally available.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: set a monthly spend cap on one agent and watch its cost per resolved conversation.

sections.title: Funding
sections.description: Rounds checked against a company or lead-investor post. Amounts for fal come from press reports.

items.title: fal closes a Series F at a $16B valuation, led by Bessemer
items.summary: fal says Sequoia led its Series E and Bessemer led its Series F. TechFundingNews and Tech.eu put the Series F at $1.3 billion and the valuation at $16 billion. fal's own posts give no amounts, so the dollar figures come from the press reports.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: price your own image and video workloads against fal's hosted models.

items.title: Trajectory raises a $45M Series A at $300M from Sequoia and opens its training platform
items.summary: Trajectory's platform shapes, trains, evaluates and deploys models that learn from customer interactions, works with any agent harness and says setup takes two code changes. Its site lists $60 million across the Series A and seed, with Fei-Fei Li and Jeff Dean as backers, and 14 deployments live in production.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: log your agent's conversations this month and score which ones were solved on the first try.

items.title: NanoForge AI raises a $10.4M seed to discover battery and semiconductor materials
items.summary: Korean startup NanoForge AI raised a $10.4 million seed led by Mirae Asset to discover next-generation materials with AI. The company is testing with Samsung Electronics and a battery maker. Science bonus applied to the score.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: list the three materials your product depends on and ask which have an AI-designed alternative in testing.

sections.title: Open Source and Science Data
sections.description: Open releases, datasets and agent tooling you can run yourself.

items.title: Gradium's Phonon speaks from a 65 MB model on phones, laptops and in the browser
items.summary: Phonon is a family of small text-to-speech models of about 65 and 75 MB that run on-device without a server, in a browser or on single-board computers. It ships with more than 100 voices. Phonon 31m is English-only under Apache 2.0, and Phonon 40m covers English, French, German, Spanish and Portuguese under CC BY-NC.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: add a spoken readout to your app or newsletter page with a model that runs in the visitor's browser.
items.pricing: Phonon 31m free for commercial use (Apache 2.0); Phonon 40m free for non-commercial use (CC BY-NC).

items.title: Ai2 ToyBlocks generates 85,336 robot demonstrations in a simulated tabletop
items.summary: ToyBlocks is an open simulation framework with a robot arm and tabletop blocks for training and evaluating robot-learning models. The release includes 85,336 demonstrations, about 1,600 hours of execution data and 144 million frames, generated up to 24 times faster than real time.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: borrow the block-stacking tasks to benchmark any robot policy you are testing.

items.title: Phone Harness lets agents tap, scroll and type on a real iPhone or Android phone
items.summary: Phone Harness is open source and has passed 4,000 GitHub stars. Agents control iPhone through iPhone Mirroring or Android through adb and read screens with vision OCR or the accessibility tree. The Basic plan is $0 with $5 of credit, Android runs 5 cents per phone-minute, and Plus is $20 a month for 1,000 minutes. The service is in open beta.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: ask an agent to book a recurring appointment through the actual app on your phone.

sections.title: To Watch
sections.description: Early programs, hardware and previews with high signal.

items.title: Perplexity Teammates are persistent agents for ongoing work, in research preview for Max subscribers
items.summary: Teammates are persistent AI agents that run inside Perplexity Computer for ongoing work. They are a research preview for individual Max subscribers on the web at $200 a month. Enterprise Pro and Enterprise Max accounts are not included by default.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: give a Teammate your weekly newsletter reading list and have it send a Friday digest.
items.pricing: Research preview for individual Max subscribers ($200 a month).

items.title: Subvocal glasses turn silent mouth movements into text at 200+ words per minute
items.summary: The Subvocal Company (YC F26) says its glasses use low-power radio sensing to decode silent articulation into text at speaking speed, with no camera or microphone. A $199 refundable deposit holds a pair at the $499 early-bird price, shipping is estimated for Q1 2027, and preorders are limited to the US. The Show HN thread reached 843 points and 395 comments.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: read the HN thread's error-rate discussion and decide which writing task you would dictate silently.

items.title: Cyclon preorders an AI phone for $199 on a Pixel 8a
items.summary: Cyclon is an AI phone that uses apps on the user's behalf, builds apps and handles notifications. The first limited batch is a Pixel 8a with Cyclon preinstalled for a $199 preorder while its own device is in development. The founders won YC's Call-My-Agent hackathon against more than 90 teams.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: list the five phone tasks you repeat daily and see which Cyclon says it covers.

items.title: World Labs Frameboy streams Atlas worlds into a browser at up to 15 fps
items.summary: Frameboy is a research preview that streams Atlas 3D worlds to the browser at up to 15 frames per second from cloud GPUs. The Viewfinder tool is in closed beta.
items.enterprise_translation: Steal this idea: open a world in the browser and use it as a moodboard for your next set or game level.

emerging_signals.pattern: Video and music tools are gaining real editors
emerging_signals.evidence: Omni 1.2 Flash adds multi-turn edits, Instagram Edits adds a desktop timeline with MCP agents, Splice Create embeds Rheo, OpusClip 4.0 ships a ChatGPT and Claude plugin, and Suno accepts MIDI.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Whether chat-based edits replace regeneration as the default way to revise a clip.

emerging_signals.pattern: Agents are getting their own devices
emerging_signals.evidence: Glasshand rents real iPhones and Macs, Phone Harness reached 4,000 stars, Cyclon preorders a Pixel-based AI phone and Raven pitches a phone for agents.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Which of these publish task-success numbers on real apps.

emerging_signals.pattern: Open science models and agent skills reach labs
emerging_signals.evidence: Hydrogen-1.0 ships MIT weights, DeepMind packages RDKit, ChEMBL and PubChem as skills, NanoForge raised $10.4M for materials, and Canos reports 91% sensitivity in dogs.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Independent replications of Hydrogen-1.0's FrontierScience-Research score.

emerging_signals.pattern: Persistent agents become a paid tier
emerging_signals.evidence: Kiro bots are generally available, Perplexity Teammates are in preview for Max, Copilot Studio adds persistent agents and Rerun sells unlimited Coworkers for $29 a month.
emerging_signals.what_to_watch: Whether pricing settles on flat monthly plans or credits.

flagged_unverified.claim: Deep Principle Hydrogen-1.0 benchmark results (38.33% on FrontierScience-Research and a 4.318 eV HOMO-LUMO gap).
flagged_unverified.reason: All figures are the company's own. The blog post is undated and the Hugging Face model card lists no benchmark scores. The November 2 release date and weights availability are supported by Deep Principle's launch post on X, dated November 2.

flagged_unverified.claim: fal's $1.3B Series F at a $16B valuation.
flagged_unverified.reason: fal's own posts name the lead investors (Sequoia for Series E, Bessemer for Series F) and give no amounts. The dollar figures come from TechFundingNews and Tech.eu.

flagged_unverified.claim: Thinking Machines Inkling 2 Small Apache 2.0 weights.
flagged_unverified.reason: The weights were closed on Tinker at launch, and the company says Apache 2.0 weights follow the next week. No release was visible by November 8.

flagged_unverified.claim: Periodic Labs $300M raise and NVIDIA Cosmos 3 releases surfaced in search results dated this week.
flagged_unverified.reason: Primary pages show dates outside November 2 to 8 or could not be dated (Cosmos 3: October 26 to 30; Periodic Labs: a November 9 date). Excluded.

flagged_unverified.claim: Splice Create pricing: whether the Free plan includes WAV and stem export.
flagged_unverified.reason: Splice's plans card lists 'Export WAV and stems' under Free, while the FAQ and Help Center say export needs a subscription (Create Pro at $9.99 a month introductory, Creator or Creator+). The summary states both and treats the subscription requirement as Splice's support position. The earlier 3-million-sample figure came from a Yahoo review; Splice's own page says 'millions', so the tab uses that wording.

suggested_refinements.notes: Source limits: Product Hunt returns 403 to uncached or automated fetches, so the weekly leaderboard was read through the page-fetch tool and figures are weekly upvotes and comments at fetch time; Tobira and Turnstone were left out because their vote counts were inconsistent (3,387 daily versus 388 weekly). OpenAI, Perplexity, Microsoft and Product Hunt pages return 403 to curl, and floot.com returns 404 to curl, so these were read through the page-fetch tool, which rendered real content for each (both OpenAI Top Pick pages confirmed with November 3 and 4 dates). YC Launch dates come from page HTML timestamps because the UI shows relative times. Hydrogen-1.0 benchmarks are self-reported and its blog post is undated; the date is supported by the company's X launch post (Nov 2). fal amounts come from press reports. Kimi K3.1 Pro is marked returning because the model was announced October 25 and the weights shipped this week. Items from Dream Labs, Opentrons, Reflection, Holo4, Amazon Bee and Karpathy's HackerTube fell before November 2 and were excluded. The floor of 20 items and the 0.85 freshness target are both met; all items are new except one.
